stem: A client with a deep contaminated traumatic wound develops rapidly worsening pain that is disproportionate to the initial skin findings, marked edema, systemic toxicity, and palpable crepitus. Which complication should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Clostridial myonecrosis (gas gangrene), requiring immediate surgical evaluation and emergency treatment.
options.B: Uncomplicated superficial cellulitis that can be managed with routine outpatient observation while culture results are pending.
options.C: Contact dermatitis from the wound dressing because crepitus is a typical finding of allergic skin inflammation.
options.D: Normal inflammatory wound healing because severe pain and rapidly progressive tissue swelling are expected after deep trauma.

rationale: A is correct. Clostridial myonecrosis is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening necrotizing infection associated with traumatic wounds. Severe pain, rapid edema/tissue progression, systemic toxicity, and soft-tissue gas or crepitus are strongly concerning findings. NCBI guidance emphasizes that diagnosis is primarily clinical and treatment should not be delayed while awaiting definitive microscopy or culture; immediate surgical treatment and antimicrobial therapy are required. B does not fit the rapid, toxic, gas-forming pattern. C does not explain tissue gas or systemic toxicity. D dangerously normalizes findings of a necrotizing infection.
educational_objective: Recognize severe pain out of proportion, rapidly progressive edema, systemic toxicity, and tissue gas/crepitus after a contaminated wound as a high-priority pattern for clostridial myonecrosis requiring immediate surgical escalation rather than delayed confirmation.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI StatPearls
source_document_title: Hyperbaric Treatment of Clostridial Myositis and Myonecrosis; Gangrene
source_version_date: Clostridial Myositis/Myonecrosis last updated May 31, 2023; Gangrene updated July 20, 2025 in StatPearls 2026 edition; pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Clostridial Myositis and Myonecrosis — Introduction: gas gangrene is life-threatening and requires immediate diagnosis/treatment. History and Physical: traumatic gas gangrene presents with sudden severe pain, massive edema, discoloration/bullae, and possible crepitus due to gas. Evaluation/Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes: diagnosis is clinical; microscopy may take time and should not delay treatment; immediate surgical treatment is required. Gangrene — Gas gangrene: rapidly progressive necrotizing infection with edema, crepitance, severe pain and systemic deterioration.
source_claim_supported: After a contaminated traumatic wound, severe disproportionate pain, rapid swelling/systemic toxicity, and crepitus should prompt immediate suspicion for clostridial myonecrosis; treatment requires urgent surgical management and antibiotics without waiting for delayed confirmatory testing.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: recognize signs and symptoms of acute client complications and intervene; Medical Emergencies content includes rapid recognition and escalation of life-threatening deterioration.
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — recognition of necrotizing soft-tissue infection/clostridial myonecrosis
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source recognition item with a clinically discriminating necrotizing-infection pattern and realistic competing interpretations. The final answer avoids implying crepitus is always present or that culture confirmation must precede emergency treatment.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against NCBI StatPearls clostridial myonecrosis and the updated 2025 Gangrene chapter.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A explains the entire rapid gas-forming toxic pattern. B undercalls a necrotizing process. C cannot explain crepitus/systemic toxicity. D falsely normalizes emergency findings.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; suspected clostridial myonecrosis requiring immediate surgical escalation.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; superficial cellulitis does not fit rapid deep-tissue gas/toxicity.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; allergic dermatitis does not produce tissue gas.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; this progression is not normal healing.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Other necrotizing soft-tissue infections can cause severe pain and gas, but the contaminated traumatic-wound context plus crepitus makes clostridial myonecrosis the best first suspicion; the item asks 'suspect first,' not definitive diagnosis.
audit_findings.cueing: All options interpret the same wound deterioration.
audit_findings.blueprint: Rapid recognition of a life-threatening complication fits Physiological Adaptation.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked necrotizing fasciitis versus gas gangrene overlap and removed any claim that crepitus is mandatory or pathogen-specific. The final pattern and wound context support A as the single best first suspicion without overclaiming microbiologic certainty.
